chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who goes hunting for one day, two days, or three: does he shorten the salat (prayer)? He said: No, unless a man is escorting his brother in religion, for hunting is a vain journey in which the salat (prayer) is not shortened. And he said: He shortens when he escorts his brother.

key_terms.أَخَاهُ فِي الدِّينِ: his brother in religion, meaning a fellow believer

ai.seo_question: Does a person shorten the salat (prayer) while traveling for hunting according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about shortening the salat (prayer) during travel undertaken for hunting. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that hunting as such is a vain journey and does not permit qaṣr, while accompanying one's believing brother is a valid purpose for which the salat (prayer) may be shortened.
